goal: Values, strings, decisions, loops and the four collections. By ten you can say exactly what any short program prints, sweep a broken listing for its errors, write a grading ladder, and name the right collection with its reason.
drill: The practice questions at the end of each lesson are the fastest way to find a gap. In Operators, the worked answer on the and operator is the one you must be able to reproduce.

window: Thursday, 10:15 am to 1:30 pm, before the paper at 3
goal: The questions that carry most of the paper: functions, modules, file handling and the SQLite database. Then sit the last paper's questions in your book before reading each model answer, and finish on the reference card.
drill: Write the seven line database skeleton and the four file modes from memory. In the hall, choose the database, file handling, functions and short-parts questions.

window: Only if you finish early: objective-half lessons and extra practice, not required
goal: Exceptions and the graphical interface are asked in the objective half only, so they come last. Then three practice papers in the shape of the real one, if there is time at all.
drill: Eat before the paper. The reference card is the last thing you read.
